target.title: fix(anthropic): interrupted thinking no longer bricks replay
target.body:
Closes #103830
Supersedes the administratively closed #103938.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an interrupted Anthropic extended-thinking stream could persist an incomplete cryptographic signature. Every later turn in that session replayed the truncated signature, causing Anthropic to reject the request and effectively making the session unusable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signature deltas are opaque and only known to be complete when the matching `content_block_stop` arrives. The transport now stages delta bytes privately by content-block index, clears the replay-visible signature when delta streaming begins, and commits the exact staged bytes only at that lifecycle boundary.

This preserves completed signatures byte-for-byte, preserves provider-seeded signatures when no delta follows, clears pending state across fallback boundaries, and avoids format, length, or cryptographic guesses about provider-owned data. Existing rejection-time repair remains available for sessions poisoned by older versions.

This change was developed with Codex assistance. I reviewed the implementation and understand the affected transport and replay behavior.

## User Impact

An interrupted Anthropic thinking response no longer poisons the session's future conversation history. Users can continue the same session after a network interruption or incomplete provider stream instead of resetting it and losing conversational context.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`
  - 107 tests passed.
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking-replay-repair.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts`
  - 199 tests passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 pnpm check:changed`
  - Passed core type checks, test type checks, changed lint, import-cycle checks, and repository guards.
- `$autoreview`
  - Clean, with no accepted or actionable findings.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`; `git range-diff` confirmed the patch remained content-identical.

All tests and live proof ran through Crabbox on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7c9m7z63hk8kcyn3vb4466`.

### Live behavior proof

A loopback fault proxy forwarded real Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 traffic, intercepted the provider's 432-byte `signature_delta`, forwarded only the first 216 bytes, and terminated the stream before `content_block_stop`.

Before the fix:

- The interrupted output persisted the 216-byte partial signature.
- The next request replayed that signature.
- Anthropic returned HTTP 400 with an invalid-signature response.

After the fix:

- The interrupted output persisted no signature delta bytes.
- The replay request and another same-session continuation contained no incomplete thinking signature.
- All three Anthropic requests returned HTTP 200 and both subsequent turns completed normally.

The live proof was executed against the committed patch before a content-preserving rebase; `git range-diff` maps that commit directly to the current PR head.

target.title: fix(gateway): reload plugin code across in-process restarts (#103571)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An in-process gateway restart (SIGUSR1 / `gateway restart --safe` under `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`) re-runs each plugin's `register()` and logs `<plugin> registered` — but serves the module graph cached from the original process start. Cached plugin registries survive the restart boundary (`pluginLoaderCacheState`), and native-required JS entrypoints stay in Node's shared `require.cache`, so updated **workspace plugin code** on disk (e.g. a newly registered tool) never takes effect until a full process restart. Config changes *do* reload because the restart iteration hook already calls `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` — plugin caches were the missing symmetric clear. Fixes #103571.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart is the repo's documented **explicit reload boundary** for process-stable plugin state ("Plugin metadata changes require restart or explicit plugin owner reload/install/doctor flow" — `src/plugins/AGENTS.md`). Add `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` in the plugins loader (drops cached registries + activated runtime state, manifest read caches, and purges previously imported plugin entrypoints from `require.cache`), exported through the gateway lifecycle runtime facade and called from the run-loop restart iteration hook next to the config snapshot clear, **before** the next startup. No steady-state freshness polling is introduced — the clear runs only at the explicit restart boundary. No new options or public API surface.

## User Impact

Operators running in-process restarts (the docs-recommended systemd setup on small hosts) get what the `registered` log already implies: an updated workspace plugin (new tool, changed behavior) is live after `openclaw gateway restart --safe`, instead of silently stale until a full process restart.

## Evidence

Two tests, both discriminating:
- `run-loop.test.ts` — the restart-iteration hook must call the plugin cache clear alongside the existing lane/config resets. **Fails on main** (`clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart` never called: `1 failed | 40 passed`), passes with this PR (41/41).
- `loader.restart-reload.test.ts` (new) — real temp workspace plugin registering `probe_tool_v1` → source+manifest edited on disk to `probe_tool_v2` → reload **without** the clear still serves v1 (reproduces the reported staleness) → reload **after** `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` loads `probe_tool_v2` from disk.

`tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix(ui): suppress login gate flash on refresh with stored token
target.body:
Closes #103342

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where refreshing the Control UI while authenticated with token auth (or any stored credentials) briefly flashed the login gate before the gateway connection finished. The flash was most noticeable behind an Nginx HTTPS reverse proxy, where the WebSocket handshake introduced a small delay, but the root cause was a race in the initial paint: the splash that should cover the first connect was only shown after the gateway client had been created, leaving a window where the login gate rendered even though credentials were present.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI's `initialConnectPending` condition required `gatewaySnapshot.client !== null` to show the connecting splash. The client is created asynchronously when `runtime.start()` calls `gateway.start()` → `connect()`, so the first paint after `connectedCallback` could render the login gate while stored credentials were already loaded.

This change introduces an `initialConnectSplashGuard` that is set when stored credentials are detected at mount and is cleared once the first connect attempt becomes observable (client created, connection opened, or an error emitted). The splash now covers the first paint through the end of the first connect attempt, eliminating the transient unauthenticated state.

## User Impact

Control UI users with stored tokens, passwords, or device tokens no longer see a forced-logout flash when refreshing the page. The experience is a smooth loading splash that transitions directly to the app shell on success or to the login gate on a real auth failure.

## Evidence

- Added unit tests in `ui/src/app/app-host.test.ts` verifying the splash guard stays active before a connect attempt is observable and is cleared when the gateway creates a client or emits an error.
- Added an E2E regression in `ui/src/e2e/initial-connect-splash.e2e.test.ts` that navigates with a stored token and asserts the splash is present on first paint before the mock gateway observes the connect request, with no `openclaw-login-gate` in the DOM.
- Ran focused tests locally:
  - `cd ui && npx vitest run app-host.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts` — 9 tests passed.
  - `npx vitest run ui/src/e2e/initial-connect-splash.e2e.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` — 5 tests passed.

target.title: fix(ui): chat workspace rail and detail panel break narrow panes and compact windows
target.body:
Closes #104023

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening the session workspace rail or the file/tool detail panel in a narrow chat pane would see the layout fall apart. The rail and detail panel keyed their layout off viewport media queries, so a narrow split-view pane inside a wide window (or a compact macOS-app session window whose webview reports a wide viewport) still got the wide side-by-side treatment: a 280px rail column crushed the thread to a ~300px sliver with clipped, overlapping bubbles, and the chat + detail-panel pair (312px + 300px minimums) overflowed the pane. Below a 1120px viewport the rail and all of its toggles were simply `display: none`, making workspace files unreachable in narrow windows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Layout decisions now follow the pane's own measured width instead of viewport breakpoints: `openclaw-chat-pane` observes its width with a `ResizeObserver` and switches to horizontal splits when side-by-side cannot fit. Below 800px of pane width the workspace rail always presents as the existing bottom-dock strip (side-dock drag/toggle controls hide until the pane widens; the persisted dock preference is untouched). When the width available to the chat + detail split (pane minus a side-docked rail) drops under 680px, the detail panel stacks below the thread and the shared `resizable-divider` flips to its horizontal orientation, so the split stays resizable. The phone-sized (≤768px viewport) full-screen detail takeover is unchanged. The 1120px hide-the-rail cliff is removed — the rail is now usable at every width — and two bottom-strip rows (workspace path, summary chips) no longer flex-shrink into clipped text.

## User Impact

Narrow chat panes — split-view panes, compact desktop windows, and macOS-app session windows — keep a readable thread when the workspace rail or detail panel is open: panels move below the chat instead of fighting it for horizontal space. Workspace files are now reachable in windows narrower than 1120px, where the rail previously did not exist at all.

## Evidence

Reproduced and verified with the Control UI mock-gateway Playwright harness (chromium + webkit) across 1440/1150/1000/900/800/700/500px windows and a two-pane split view; a geometry probe asserts no rail/thread/panel rect intersections and no horizontal document overflow at any size after the change.

target.title: fix(release): reconcile contribution provenance
target.body:
Closes #103429

> Draft/HOLD: do not merge until the immutable historical reconciliation passes
> on exact signed head `94ff88960d7b52409c4dc9ce75e274fa73f4deac`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where release maintainers could generate an incomplete
contribution record because the verifier treated first-parent history as the
source inventory and allowed contextual references to stand in for source-PR
ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The verifier now inventories the complete raw Git DAG from the unique merge
base, rejects shallow/grafted/replaced history, and assigns each commit through
auditable GitHub associations, strict merged-PR directives, exact/partial/
adapted provenance, verified revert parity, or direct-commit classification.
It records canonical/current/generated/missing/stale sets, compares the
canonical inventory with the complete merged-main GitHub universe, and accepts
only a bounded association-free `CHANGELOG.md` tail after the immutable product
cutoff.

Ledger output is transactional and fail-closed: a pending sentinel replaces any
stale pass before fallible verifier work, output uses sibling temp-file renames,
rollback preserves the pending sentinel, concurrent writers are not overwritten,
and dangling symlink aliases to `CHANGELOG.md` are rejected. Consumers must
verify the current successful invocation plus the actual changelog and release
section hashes; `status: "pass"` alone is not acceptance evidence.

## User Impact

Release maintainers get a deterministic, fail-closed contribution manifest with
complete source-PR credit, direct-commit auditability, explicit
shipped/reverted exclusions, immutable evidence hashes, and concrete
reconciliation metrics before publication.

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators can get stuck in a gateway restart death-loop for the same wedged main session. After the gateway restarts, a persisted aborted main session can keep entering automatic restart recovery instead of being stopped once accepted recovery attempts show that the session needs operator inspection.

The user-visible failure mode is repeated automatic main-session resume across gateway boots, including slow loops where cron/systemd backoff leaves more than a few minutes between recovery attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the durable stop-condition direction from the existing PR and makes main-session restart recovery use an accepted-attempt fuse that is reset by successful progress, not by elapsed time:

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` state with `automaticAttempts`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastRunId`, `wedgedAt`, and `wedgedReason`.
- Reuses the shared `restart-recovery-fuse` helper; main-session recovery now evaluates cumulative accepted attempts with no time-window expiry, while subagent recovery keeps its existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Reserves the durable fuse before dispatching the gateway recovery run, then replaces the provisional idempotency key with the accepted run id.
- Rolls back the provisional fuse reservation when gateway dispatch fails before acceptance.
- Records the accepted recovery run id in `restartRecoveryRuns` for lifecycle suppression, while using `mainRestartRecovery` as the primary retry fuse.
- Keeps a legacy marker-derived attempt floor for old rows that already contain `restartRecoveryRuns` but do not yet have `mainRestartRecovery`.
- Accepted recovery run completion now persists its terminal lifecycle patch and clears main restart-recovery state, so a successfully recovered session gets a new automatic recovery budget later.
- Exhausted rows are tombstoned before another resume dispatch, clear `abortedLastRun`, and transition the session to `failed` with terminal timing fields.
- When an exhausted row still has a restart-recovery delivery route, the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice is sent before the row is tombstoned.
- Transcript preflight/read failures do not create durable recovery state, and pre-acceptance gateway dispatch failures roll back provisional reservations.
- Existing subagent recovery state remains owned by subagent recovery; ordinary main/session progress clears stale main restart-recovery state but does not clear `subagentRecovery`.
- The existing in-process `MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES` remains a transient startup retry/backoff guard and is not the durable cross-boot policy.

Contract and risk note:

- This intentionally changes main-session restart recovery from a two-minute rapid re-wedge budget to a cumulative accepted-attempt budget since the last successful main-session completion. The reason is the linked issue's cross-boot death-loop shape: a 5-minute cron loop or longer systemd backoff should still consume the same durable budget and tombstone before another automatic resume.
- The compatibility boundary is that successful run completion and ordinary user progress clear `mainRestartRecovery`, so healthy sessions do not permanently lose automatic recovery capacity after one bad boot sequence.
- Subagent orphan recovery intentionally does not adopt this broader contract; it keeps its existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.

Boundaries and non-goals:

- This adds only an optional internal `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` persistence field for main restart recovery. It does not add public config, wire protocol, credentials/auth behavior, provider discovery behavior, or Telegram/systemd runtime behavior.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle-suppression and legacy-floor state; it is no longer the primary retry fuse for newly accepted recoveries.
- This does not add a new full Telegram/systemd/live-provider loop proof in this local environment. The PR already carries the prior Mantis Telegram Desktop gateway-run proof from the PR discussion, and this update adds issue-specific file-backed runtime coverage through the production restart-recovery entrypoint.
- Another open candidate was visible for the same issue; this update repairs the existing contributor PR and leaves final landing-path choice to maintainers.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable automatic recovery stop condition across gateway restarts. A wedged main session that accepts two automatic recovery dispatches since the last successful completion is tombstoned before a third automatic resume, even when attempts are separated by a five-minute cron loop or longer systemd backoff.

After inspection or successful recovery, normal main-session progress clears stale main restart-recovery metadata so a healthy later reboot gets a fresh budget without erasing independent subagent recovery tombstones.

- Real behavior proof:

target.title: feat(google-meet): retain the full caption transcript per session (#103387)
target.body:
## Summary

Implements #103387.

The Chrome transport scrapes Meet captions into an in-page buffer capped at 50 lines, and `status` exposed only the last 5 as `recentTranscript` — so for any real meeting the transcript was mostly discarded, and observe-mode users had to build fragile external pollers that still lose lines during fast speech. This follows the accumulation design proposed in the issue.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/chrome.ts`: the status script now also ships its full in-page buffer as `transcriptWindow` (≤50 lines); `recentTranscript` stays at 5 lines for compatibility.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: the gateway merges `transcriptWindow` into a durable per-session transcript on every health refresh (join + status/health polls), deduped by the page-recorded `at`/`speaker`/`text` key, capped at the most recent **2000 lines** (fixed constant — no new config surface per the repo's config bar; `droppedLines` reports trimming). The window is merge input only and is stripped before health lands in status payloads, so `status` responses stay the same size. New `transcript(sessionId, { sinceIndex? })` refreshes browser health for active sessions and returns lines with absolute indices: `nextIndex` from one call is the `sinceIndex` for the next, which fixes the issue's "poll gap" problem exactly.
- `extensions/google-meet/index.ts`: new `googlemeet.transcript` gateway method and `transcript` tool action with optional `sinceIndex`.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts`: `openclaw googlemeet transcript <session-id> [--since <index>] [--json]`.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: observe-only section + tool action table updated.

Not included (flagged in the issue as optional): `chrome.transcriptFile` persistence — repo storage policy points that at SQLite rather than a JSONL sidecar, which is a separate product decision.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 207 tests passed. New regressions: overlapping page windows across polls accumulate without duplicates and the `sinceIndex` cursor returns exactly zero new lines at `nextIndex`; the cap test proves 2100 merged lines yield `droppedLines: 100`, retained lines 100..2099 in order (this test caught and fixed a dedupe-eviction bug during development); status payload health carries no `transcriptWindow`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt, oxlint — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: caption lines beyond a 5-line window over a 50-line page buffer were irrecoverable; no way to retrieve a meeting transcript after the fact.
Real environment tested: the plugin's real join/status/transcript gateway methods driven through the existing stubbed browser-proxy harness, with the page status script's real JSON contract (including the new `transcriptWindow`) exercised end to end.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet`
Evidence after fix: joining with page windows `[1..3]` then polling with `[2..5]` yields transcript lines 1..5 exactly once with `nextIndex: 5`; `sinceIndex: 5` returns no lines; a 2100-line window yields `droppedLines: 100` with lines 100..2099 retained in order.
Observed result after fix: 207/207 tests pass; the transcript survives beyond the page window and is retrievable incrementally via CLI, gateway method, and tool action.
What was not tested: a live Google Meet call with real captions; the merge consumes the same parsed status payload shape the live path produces, and the page-side change is a one-line widening of what the existing scraper already records.

target.title: fix(macos): reject revoked forwarded exec approvals
target.body:
Depends on #103950

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where delayed Gateway approval for a Mac App node could be rebound to freshly evaluated Mac policy. A rule revoked after upstream approval could therefore be restored by a later allow-always commit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node host now carries the canonical persisted-policy snapshot through both Mac execution routes: the authenticated exec socket and the native node session. The Mac requires the original snapshot for forwarded explicit and auto-review authority, revalidates it under the approval-store write lock, and rejects changed mutable script operands before execution.

Gateway no longer synthesizes delayed authority for nodes that omit `system.run.prepare`. It cannot prove remote executable or file identity from its own filesystem, so approval-requiring legacy native runs now fail closed before approval registration. Direct full/off execution remains unchanged.

Legacy boolean approvals normalize to one-shot socket decisions, and legacy allowlist source strings normalize to the portable `allow-always` contract before Swift decoding.

## User Impact

Mac App and CLI nodes now reject delayed approvals when policy is revoked while approval is in flight. Native nodes without prepare support receive a clear fail-closed error for approval-requiring runs instead of an unsafe Gateway-local plan. Local prompts, current-policy execution, ask-fallback ownership, and direct full/off execution are unchanged.

## Evidence

- clawmac native macOS run: 147 tests across five approval/runtime suites passed, including policy revocation, changed-script rejection, restored-byte execution, plan identity, and denial behavior.
- Follow-up native clawmac run: 115 tests across `ExecApprovalsStoreRefactorTests` and `MacNodeRuntimeTests` passed.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true

target.title: fix(cli): avoid zero usage cost during cache refresh
target.body:
Fixes #103882

AI-assisted: Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw gateway usage-cost --all-agents` could see `$0` during a cold aggregate-cache rebuild even though agent usage data existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway intentionally rebuilds aggregate cost caches in the background so large histories do not block a request for minutes. This keeps that behavior intact and makes the explicit CLI audit command poll with exponential backoff until the cache is settled, with a bounded five-minute timeout. Gateway protocol and Control UI behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

`gateway usage-cost` now prints settled totals once the cache rebuild completes, or exits with a clear timeout error instead of presenting a transient zero as the final result.

## Evidence

- Real CLI-to-Gateway before/after proof reproduced the transient zero on current `main` and returned settled nonzero totals on runtime commit `db846cf6d421`. Current head `594336c6ca1` changes only the regression test's callback typing; production content is identical.
- The regression test drives the real CLI command through the real `usage.cost` handler with two real agent transcripts. It observes `refreshing` first, `fresh` last, and verifies the final aggregate is `100` tokens / `$0.10`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts` — 2 files, 37 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -t 'rebuilds cold durable aggregate cache synchronously when requested'` — 1 passed, 68 skipped.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-103998-core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed after binding the regression callback to the real handler type.
- `oxfmt --check` and scoped `oxlint` passed for both changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- One pre-commit autoreview round completed with no actionable findings.
- Sanitized remote proof was unavailable because Crabbox has no configured coordinator, while credential-hydrated Testbox is intentionally disallowed for fork source. The documented narrow local fallback below used isolated, non-sensitive state.

### Real CLI ↔ Gateway proof

Setup: two fresh isolated state directories with no durable usage cache, two synthetic agents (`main` = 30 tokens / `$0.03`, `dev` = 70 tokens / `$0.07`), loopback-only `auth.mode=none`, and no provider credentials or calls. Each side ran a real foreground Gateway plus a separate real CLI process over WebSocket through the source-checkout entry (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`). Daily rows are omitted below; the shown totals and cache status are copied from the command output.

Current `main` at `f4b3a4841f2`, first cold request:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --all-agents --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 0, "totalCost": 0 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "refreshing",
    "cachedFiles": 0,
    "pendingFiles": 2,
    "staleFiles": 2
  }
}
```

PR runtime commit `db846cf6d421` (production-identical to current head `594336c6ca1`), first request against an equivalent cold state:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --all-agents --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 100, "totalCost": 0.1 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "fresh",
    "cachedFiles": 2,
    "pendingFiles": 0,
    "staleFiles": 0
  }
}
```

Representative explicit-agent request on the same PR Gateway:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --agent main --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 30, "totalCost": 0.03 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "fresh",
    "cachedFiles": 1,
    "pendingFiles": 0,
    "staleFiles": 0
  }
}
```

target.title: fix(google): Veo video generation fails with google-prefixed model ids
target.body:
Closes #103291

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where calling `video_generate` with a Google Veo model (e.g. `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`) fails with `API_KEY_INVALID` from the GenAI SDK, even though the same API key succeeds against the direct REST `predictLongRunning` endpoint with the `instances[].prompt` schema.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runtime already strips the `google/` provider prefix before forwarding the model id to the provider, so the provider receives the bare model name. The remaining failure is at the provider/SDK boundary: the GenAI SDK path for Veo models returns auth-style errors, while the existing REST fallback (which uses the correct `predictLongRunning` endpoint and schema) works.

This change:
1. Normalizes `google/`, `google/models/`, and `models/` prefixes to a bare Veo model id so both SDK and REST paths construct the correct `models/veo-...` URL.
2. Falls back to the REST `predictLongRunning` path for **any** SDK failure when the model is a Veo model and the request is text-only (the same condition that already allowed 404 fallback).

## User Impact

`video_generate` with `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, `google/models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, or `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` now routes through the working REST endpoint instead of failing on the broken SDK path.

## Evidence

### Shared-runtime regression

Added `src/video-generation/runtime.test.ts` regression verifying that the shared runtime strips the provider prefix from `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` and forwards the bare model id `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` to the provider.

Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/runtime.test.ts` — 29 tests passed.

### Provider behavior proof (SDK failure → REST success)

Added `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts` regression verifying that when the GenAI SDK rejects a Veo request with `API_KEY_INVALID` (status 400), the provider falls back to REST and hits `models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning` with the `instances[].prompt` schema, returning the generated video successfully.

Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts` — 19 tests passed.

### Direct-provider URL before/after

Intercepted the real provider code path with a stubbed API key and logged the outgoing URL:

**Before this change** (reverting to `HEAD~1`):
```text
[URL-PROOF] https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
```

**After this change** (current branch, `google/veo-...` normalized):
```text
[URL-PROOF] https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
```

The API key was redacted; no account, private endpoint, IP, or project id appears in the output.

### Note on live end-to-end proof

I do not have a live Google API key in this environment, so the before/after above exercises the real provider code path with intercepted HTTP. A maintainer with a Google key can verify by running `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test extensions/google/google.live.test.ts` or a live `video_generate` call.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above

target.title: fix(memory): skip blank search provider bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory search handled blank or whitespace-only queries too late. The manager could initialize the provider, assert provider state, or bootstrap search work before the preflight returned an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blank query eligibility is a local preflight contract and should not require provider setup. This change shares query normalization with the existing preflight and short-circuits blank queries before provider/bootstrap work.

## User Impact

Whitespace-only memory searches return `[]` cheaply and deterministically, without requiring provider credentials, indexes, or search startup.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`.
- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.ts`.
- Added `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts` proving blank search returns `[]` before provider init, provider assertion, index check, or sync bootstrap.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Controlled manager proof: `node --import tsx - <<'EOF' ...` invoked the actual `MemoryIndexManager.search` method with a whitespace-only query and provider/bootstrap counters.

## Proof

- Controlled proof query: whitespace-only.
- Controlled proof result: `resultCount: 0`, `results: []`.
- Provider/bootstrap counters all stayed zero: `ensureProviderInitialized: 0`, `assertRequiredProviderAvailable: 0`, `hasIndexedContent: 0`, `sync: 0`.
- This proves the blank-query preflight returns before provider initialization, provider availability assertion, index checks, or sync bootstrap.

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Recovery is now bounded on both axes flagged in review:

- **Thread response size.** `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` requests only the newest `historyLimit + 1` posts via `?per_page=<limit>&direction=up`, then restores ascending chronological order. `GET /posts/{id}/thread` returns the entire thread by default (Mattermost `per_page=0`), so an unbounded thread would otherwise allocate and parse on the inbound path.
- **Marker lifecycle.** Backfill tracking uses one marker per thread history key (`Map<historyKey, sessionId>`) instead of a process-lifetime `Set` of `historyKey:session` compound keys. Marker memory and lookup cost stay bounded to live threads instead of accumulating an entry per session rotation and scanning the whole set on each candidate. The stored session id is read only after the admission gates, so dropped pre-admission posts never touch the session store.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests, unbounded thread fetches, or unbounded per-session marker growth on long-lived monitors.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: **3 files, 112 passed**. Covers stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, dropped pre-admission posts, adopt-pending-marker without blocking later rotation, and the initially-missing session entry path.
- Bounded fetch asserted (`client.test.ts`): a limited call issues `?per_page=2&direction=up` and re-sorts ascending so callers still build history oldest-first.
- Bounded marker asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): the backfill requests `historyLimit + 1`, and `threadBackfillMarkers.get(historyKey)` carries the current session marker across the rotation / no-refetch / no-retry / adopt paths.

The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock-mantle): dedupe the IAM token-failure diagnostic per region (#67288)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #67288. On hosts with no usable AWS credentials (Raspberry Pi installs, default Docker images), the `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin attempts IAM bearer-token generation on every implicit-discovery call (every catalog refresh) and logs `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` **every time** it fails. The user-visible symptom is continuous log noise on installs that never configured AWS.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix dedupes the failure diagnostic per region for the process lifetime instead of gating the IAM chain itself:

- `generateBearerTokenFromIam` keeps running the AWS default credential chain on every call — hosts that rely on late-arriving credentials (instance roles, IRSA, SSO) still start working the moment the chain succeeds, with no opt-in config.
- The `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` debug line is emitted **at most once per region per process** (`iamTokenFailureLogged` set). A successful token generation for that region clears the marker, so a later regression logs again.

An earlier revision of this PR short-circuited discovery entirely when no AWS env creds were present; that approach was **abandoned after review** because it broke instance-role/IRSA/SSO hosts whose credentials are not visible in env vars. The current diff contains no credential gate and adds no config surface.

**Operator-observability tradeoff (explicit):** for a region that keeps failing, only the *first* failure's details are logged per process. If the underlying failure reason later changes (e.g. from "no credentials" to a network error) while generation keeps failing, the new details are not logged until a token generation succeeds for that region or the gateway process restarts. This trades per-request detail freshness for eliminating unbounded per-request log spam.

## User Impact

- Installs without AWS credentials see the diagnostic once per region instead of on every request.
- Hosts with working or late-arriving IAM chains are unaffected: token generation is still attempted every call.
- No config changes, no new keys, no behavior change for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` users or explicit `discovery.enabled: false`.

## Evidence

Exact-head (c0e8c4d134b) regression run:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts

 ✓ logs 'IAM token generation unavailable' at most once per region across repeated implicit-discovery calls (#67288)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

The regression drives the production `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` three times with a failing token provider and asserts, via a captured discovery-subsystem logger, that:
- the token provider factory ran on **all 3** calls (IAM-chain fallback semantics preserved — no short-circuit), and
- the `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` diagnostic was emitted **exactly once**, with the expected `region` metadata — removing the dedupe guard fails the test.

Not yet supplied: redacted current-head runtime logs from a real credential-less host showing the single diagnostic across repeated catalog refreshes (the remaining reviewer ask).

target.title: fix(auth): refresh OAuth tokens inside pre-expiry margin
target.body:
Fixes #103846

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with Anthropic OAuth credentials would silently skip token refresh while still inside the intended pre-expiry refresh window: the auth manager decided a refresh was required, took the refresh lock, then the shared OAuth helper returned the unchanged credential without calling the provider token endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

`getOAuthApiKey` only refreshed after the stored `expires` timestamp had fully elapsed, while `hasUsableOAuthCredential` treats credentials as unusable once they are within the shared 5-minute margin. This change makes `getOAuthApiKey` use the same pre-expiry margin by default (with optional override/disable) so manager-driven refresh actually attempts a provider refresh instead of no-opping.

## User Impact

Anthropic (and other built-in OAuth providers routed through `getOAuthApiKey`) refresh earlier and more reliably near expiry, reducing silent keep-using-stale-token windows that the auth manager already intended to close.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Commands:
```text
# Before fix (repro on origin/main): manager needs refresh, but getOAuthApiKey no-ops
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.repro.test.ts
# OBSERVED
# {"managerSaysNeedsRefresh":true,"networkRefreshCallWasMade":false,"returnedAccessSameAsStale":true,"returnedExpiresSameAsStale":true}

# After fix
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
# 5 tests passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/anthropic.test.ts
# 12 tests passed
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
```

Focused margin suite result after patch:
```text
 ✓ |unit| src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts (5 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: When an Anthropic OAuth credential is inside the 5-minute pre-expiry margin, manager-driven refresh must call the provider refresh path and persist updated credentials (not silently return the stale credential).
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout on `fix/103846-oauth-refresh-margin`, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (provider token endpoint stubbed; manager/lock/store paths real).
- Current-main contrast: With `refreshMarginMs: 0` (main-era helper contract), the same inside-margin credential returns unchanged access and never calls `refreshToken` (`mainEraNoOpAccess: "stale-access-margin"`). After this patch, the default-margin helper + manager path refreshes and persists.
- Exact steps after patch:
  1. Seed auth profile store with Anthropic OAuth `expires = now + 4m` (inside `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS`).
  2. Assert `hasUsableOAuthCredential` → false (manager needs refresh).
  3. Control: `getOAuthApiKey(..., { refreshMarginMs: 0 })` → no network refresh, stale access returned.
  4. Run `createOAuthManager.resolveOAuthAccess` with production-shaped `refreshCredential` that calls real `getOAuthApiKey`.
  5. Assert provider `refreshToken` called once, API key is fresh, and reloaded store has new access/refresh/expires.
- Command:
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-margin.manager-path.proof.test.ts
# ✓ 1 passed
# [oauth-margin-proof] result: {
#   "managerNeedsRefresh": true,
#   "networkRefreshCallWasMade": true,
#   "returnedApiKey": "fresh-access-margin",
#   "mainEraNoOpAccess": "stale-access-margin",
#   "persistedAccess": "fresh-access-margin",
#   "marginMs": 300000
# }
```
- Focused helper suite (still green):
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
# 5 tests passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/anthropic.test.ts
# 12 tests passed
```
- Evidence after fix: manager-path proof logs `networkRefreshCallWasMade: true` and `persistedAccess: "fresh-access-margin"`; main-era control remains a no-op.
- Control check: `refreshMarginMs: 0` / outside-margin cases still skip refresh; fully elapsed expiry still refreshes; constant alignment test keeps helper margin == auth-profiles default.
- Observed result after fix: inside-margin manager refresh is no longer a silent no-op; credentials are refreshed and persisted under the real lock/store path.
- What was not tested: Live Anthropic token endpoint exchange over the public network; multi-agent cross-store mirror races (covered by sibling oauth.mirror-refresh tests).

target.body:
Closes #103694

AI-assisted contribution.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using remote MCP servers would see repeated WARN-level startup noise when a tool schema used an informational, non-standard JSON Schema `format` such as `google-duration`.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now strips only unknown schema `format` values before non-draft MCP schemas reach the SDK AJV validator. Known AJV formats such as `email`, `uri`, and date/time formats remain in place, so this removes the noisy warning without disabling standard format validation. Existing draft-2020-12 handling keeps its current format-stripping behavior.

## User Impact

Remote MCP servers with vendor-specific schema formats can load without polluting boot logs with duplicate warnings, while normal schema validation still catches invalid values for supported standard formats.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the underlying AJV behavior locally: compiling a schema with `format: "google-duration"` emits duplicate `unknown format` warnings while still validating successfully.
- Added a regression test proving `google-duration` no longer calls `console.warn` and that a known `email` format still rejects invalid input.
- Validation run:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`
  - Passed: 1 file, 43 tests.
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`
  - Both passed.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
